evals.prompt: Design a fuzz testing strategy for our student registration API endpoint. It accepts: name (string, 1-100 chars), email (valid email format), age (integer 5-120), and enrollment_date (ISO date). Generate fuzzing categories.
evals.expected_output: Proposes boundary values, format violations, injection payloads, Unicode edge cases, and overflow attempts for each field, with prioritized campaign plan.
assertions: Defines boundary value fuzz inputs for each field (e.g., 0-char name, 101-char name, age 4, age 121)
Includes format violation inputs (malformed email, invalid date formats, non-integer age)
Proposes injection payloads (SQL injection in name, XSS in email, command injection)

evals.prompt: Design property-based tests for our grade calculation function. It takes a list of scores (0-100 each) with weights (must sum to 1.0) and returns a weighted average. Define the invariants.
evals.expected_output: Defines key properties: result always 0-100, weighted average monotonicity, empty list handling, weight normalization verification.
assertions: Defines the property that the result is always between min(scores) and max(scores)
Tests that weights must sum to 1.0 and the function handles violation gracefully
Includes edge case properties: single score, all identical scores, empty score list

evals.prompt: Use AI-driven generative testing to discover edge cases in our quiz timer system. The timer counts down from a configurable duration (1-180 minutes), pauses on tab switch, and auto-submits on expiry. No tests exist today.
evals.expected_output: Proposes generative test scenarios: rapid pause/resume, timezone changes during quiz, system clock manipulation, network disconnection at expiry, concurrent timers.
assertions: Generates test scenarios for rapid pause/resume cycling
Proposes edge cases around time boundaries (expiry at exact second, clock skew, DST changes)
Includes scenarios for system-level disruptions (network loss, tab crash, battery death during quiz)

evals.prompt: Our test suite has 85% line coverage but a critical bug in production was missed: when two students submit the same quiz simultaneously, their scores get swapped. Design generative tests to catch concurrency bugs.
evals.expected_output: Proposes concurrent execution testing, race condition generators, identifies that line coverage misses concurrency issues, designs stress and interleaving tests.
assertions: Identifies that line coverage is insufficient for detecting concurrency bugs
Proposes concurrent submission generators that simulate simultaneous requests
Designs assertion strategies to verify data isolation between concurrent operations

evals.prompt: Generate a comprehensive fuzz campaign for our file upload endpoint. It accepts PDFs (max 10MB), images (PNG/JPG, max 5MB), and CSV files for bulk student import. Focus on discovering crashes and security vulnerabilities.
evals.expected_output: Proposes malformed file headers, oversized files, polyglot files, path traversal filenames, zip bombs disguised as valid formats, and MIME type mismatches.
assertions: Proposes malformed file content with valid extensions (corrupted PDF headers, truncated images)
Includes path traversal and filename injection attacks (../../etc/passwd.pdf)
Tests MIME type mismatches and polyglot files (e.g., PDF containing embedded scripts)
